spans.s:
kṣa, as collateral form of √1kṣi in kṣa-tra,
and as vbl of the same, w. the mg ‘abiding,
situate,’ in antari-kṣa.
√kṣā (kṣā́yati [761d 1]; kṣāṇá). burn.

kṣaṇa, m. instant; moment; -eṇa, -āt,
as advs [1112b, 1114b], instantly. [prob.
‘the time of a glance,’ a shortened form
of īkṣ-aṇa, ‘glance’: for mg, cf. Eng.
“in the twinkling of an eye,” and Ger.
Augen-blick, ‘glance of an eye, i. e. moment.
’]
kṣaṇika, f. -ī, a. momentary. [kṣaṇa.]
kṣatá, ppl. of √kṣan.

kṣatrá, n.
 —1. rule, dominion, power,
86^20;
 —2. later, the temporal power, imperium
(as distinguished from the spiritual
power, bráhman, ‘sacerdotium’); the
[]
second or princely caste or a member of
it. [from kṣa = √1kṣi 2: cf. kṣatra-pa,
‘governor of a dominion, satrap,’ and the
borrowed σατρά-πης.]

kṣatra-bandhu, m. one who belongs to
the kṣatra or second caste.

kṣatríya, m.
 —1. ruler, 75^1;
 —2. one
who belongs to the kṣatra or princely
caste, a Kshatriya, 57^16N. [kṣatra, 1214a.]

kṣantavya, grdv. to be put up with or
pardoned. [√kṣam, 212.]

kṣapā́, f. night. [cf. σκέπω, ‘cover,’
ψέφας, ‘darkness’: for ψ, cf. √kṣar.]

kṣapāha, n. a night and day, νυχθήμερον.
[2aha, 1253b.]

kṣamá, a. patient; bearing or enduring;
and so, equal to a thing, able. [√kṣam.]
kṣamā, f. patience; long-suffering. [do.]
1kṣáya, m. dwelling-place. [√1kṣi.]
2kṣaya, m. destruction; decay. [√2kṣi.]

√kṣar (kṣárati, -te; cakṣā́ra; ákṣār
[890]; kṣaritá).
 —1. flow;
 —2. liquefy;
melt away; and so, perish. [for *skar:
cf. ψείρω (*σπείρω) = φθείρω, ‘destroy,’
ἐ-φθάρ-η, ‘perished’: for ψ, cf. kṣapā,
kṣíti: for φθ, cf. 2kṣi.]
kṣara, a. perishable. [√kṣar.]

kṣāra, a. pungent; saline. [√kṣā: cf.
ξηρό-ς, ‘dry’: for mg, cf. Eng. caustic, lit.
‘burning,’ fig. ‘pungent.’]
